newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Police say Albanian students in south can protest.
newsitem.headline: Police say Albanian students in south can protest.

text.p: Students staging an anti-government protest in the southern town of Gjirokaster appeared to have scored a minor victory on Friday after police acknowledged their action was legal.

Albanian state-run television reported that police in the town, 230 km (145 miles) south of Tirana, had declared a hunger strike by 43 students and the occupation of a university building by some 600 others a legal protest.
Units of uniformed police and plain-clothes officers had surrounded the main university building on Thursday night and threatened to force the students to vacate the building.
The students barricaded themselves in lecture rooms, piling chairs and tables against doors and entrances. Police later withdrew.

On Friday, a thin cordon of police could be seen in front of the university and officers made no move to prevent hundreds of workers from a local shoe factory from gathering in front of the building, eyewitnesses said.
Other police officers could be seen milling around streets adjacent to the university.

Some 700 factory workers and around 1,000 residents of the town called for the resignation of Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi's government in protest at its handling of a huge savings scandal which has left thousands destitute.

Some protesters attempted to approach the windows of the university room where students are on hunger strike but were escorted away by police. Others remained on steps leading up to the university entrance.

Gjirokaster students began their action in solidarity with students on their ninth day on hunger strike in the southern town of Vlore, where thousands have marched in the streets for the past three weeks.
